newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Hesse - Buba must demand strict EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Hesse - Buba must demand strict EMU criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse said on Tuesday that the Bundesbank had no choice but to insist on strict interpretation of the Maastricht criteria for joining European Economic and Monetary Union.
Hesse, who is also president of the state central bank of Lower Saxony and Bremen, went on to say that the political room to manoeuvre on the EMU criteria was very narrow.

Hesse said in the text of a speech prepared for delivery in Hanover that a strict interpretation of the criteria was necessary, even if it meant that Germany was not among the countries qualifying for EMU membership in the first round at the start of 1999.

There was no question of ruling out Germany from EMU membership if Germany's budget deficit was 3.01 percent rather than 3,00 percent. The limit in the Maastricht Treaty for budget deficits for would-be EMU members is three percent.
After that it was a question of where to draw the line between a conceivable level and an inconceivable level, Hesse said.
Germany has always maintained a hardline approach to the interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty criteria.
At a separate event, finance ministry official Klaus Regling said Germany would not tolerate the participation of nations with an excessively high budget deficit.
"I can't expect Germany would allow a nation to participate with a budget deficit at 3.5 percent," Regling said at an economic forum in Frankfurt.
